title: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD)
summary: Maple syrup urine disease means the body cannot break down some building blocks of protein. They build up in the blood, and the urine can smell sweet, like maple syrup.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (BCKDHA, BCKDHB or DBT) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A baby with two changed copies has MSUD. Signs usually start in the first days of life. Found early, it is managed with a special diet and close care from a specialist team for life.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has MSUD. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for MSUD involve?

carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Managed with a special diet and specialist care from early on.
care: Specialist metabolic clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
